source.title_on_document: Delayed AI Access: Mitigating the Homogenising Effects of Generative AI in Collaborative Problem-Solving

paper_design_summary: Methods report random assignment of 36 graduate students to immediate GenAI access, GenAI access after 15 minutes of unassisted work, or no GenAI access, although the abstract calls the design quasi-experimental (PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 3, III. Methodology). Students worked in 13 collaborative groups (4 Immediate AI, 4 Delayed AI, 5 No AI) to develop a sustainable water plan for a touristic city in the French Rivera (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2). Final group solutions were scored for homogenisation using thematic-idea overlap across all groups; no separate creativity score is reported (PDF pp. 3-4, IV. Results).

studies.label: Collaborative problem solving with immediate, delayed, or no AI access

assignment.what_was_assigned: Graduate students were randomly assigned to immediate AI access, delayed AI access, or no AI access. The text identifies students as assigned and then describes their division into collaborative groups; the randomization procedure and its relationship to group formation are not explained. The abstract labels the design quasi-experimental, in contrast to the explicit Methods statement.
assignment.quote: A total of 36 graduate students were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions.
assignment.locator: Zenodo author-deposited PDF, p. 3, III. Methodology, opening paragraph and Fig. 2; compare p. 1, Abstract.

arms.name: Immediate AI
arms.description: GenAI access from the start, available continuously throughout the collaborative activity (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

arms.name: Delayed AI
arms.description: GenAI access introduced after 15 minutes of unassisted ideation and discussion (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

arms.name: No AI
arms.description: No GenAI access throughout the collaborative activity (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

participants.exclusions: Exclusions, analyzed-person totals, and per-arm people counts are not stated in the full text. The paper reports 36 graduate students randomly assigned; collaborative-group counts are not people counts (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology; pp. 3-4, IV. Results).
participants.who: Graduate students working in collaborative groups; field of study not stated.
participants.quote: A total of 36 graduate students were randomly assigned to one of three experimental conditions.
participants.locator: Zenodo author-deposited PDF, p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2.

ai_tool.how_used: Immediate AI groups had continuous GenAI access throughout collaboration; Delayed AI groups gained access after 15 minutes of unassisted ideation and discussion; No AI groups had no access. The model, interface, prompts, and detailed interaction procedure are not specified (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

task.description: Collaboratively develop a sustainable water plan for a touristic city in the French Rivera, balancing economic growth with environmental preservation; final group solutions were compared for thematic overlap (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and IV. Results).
task.duration: Total activity duration not stated; Delayed AI access began after 15 minutes of unassisted work (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2).

outcomes.name: Homogenisation score of solutions
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Content analysis identifies unique thematic ideas across all groups, counts how many groups share each idea, and sums the shared-idea counts for each group's homogenisation score. Higher homogenisation means less diversity. Descriptives summarize 4 Immediate AI, 4 Delayed AI, and 5 No AI groups; these are team counts, not people counts. Figure 3 presents pooled thematic-category frequencies underlying the same overlap analysis (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology, IV. Results and Figs. 2-3; p. 4, IV. Results).

contrasts.reported: Immediate AI homogenisation M = 33.250, SD = 7.932 (n = 4 groups); No AI M = 17.800, SD = 8.379 (n = 5 groups). Counts are groups, not people. Direction is coded on diversity, the inverse of homogenisation. The abstract describes Immediate AI solutions as significantly more similar, but no numerical inferential test is reported.
contrasts.locator: Zenodo author-deposited PDF, p. 1, Abstract (verbal significance claim); p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2 (group counts), IV. Results and Fig. 4; p. 4, IV. Results.

contrasts.reported: Delayed AI homogenisation M = 26.250, SD = 4.272 (n = 4 groups); No AI M = 17.800, SD = 8.379 (n = 5 groups). Counts are groups, not people. Direction is coded on diversity, the inverse of homogenisation, from the descriptive means; no numerical inferential test is reported.
contrasts.locator: Zenodo author-deposited PDF, p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2 (group counts); pp. 3-4, IV. Results and Fig. 4 (homogenisation).

contrasts.reported: Delayed AI homogenisation M = 26.250, SD = 4.272 (n = 4 groups); Immediate AI M = 33.250, SD = 7.932 (n = 4 groups). Counts are groups, not people. Results describe Delayed AI as having a significantly lower homogenisation score, but give no numerical inferential test. Direction is coded on diversity, the inverse of homogenisation.
contrasts.locator: Zenodo author-deposited PDF, p. 3, III. Methodology and Fig. 2 (group counts); pp. 3-4, IV. Results and Fig. 4 (homogenisation).

diversity_detail.metric: For each collaborative group, the sum of shared-idea counts across its thematic ideas; higher scores indicate more homogenisation.
diversity_detail.computed_over: Thematic ideas from the final products of all 13 collaborative groups, pooled across all three conditions; each group's score reflects sharing with groups in this common pool, not only groups in its own condition (PDF p. 3, IV. Results).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Group-level SDs and boxplots are reported. Despite verbal significance claims, no inferential method, numerical test statistic, p value, standard error, confidence interval, or standardized effect is supplied (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3-4, IV. Results and Fig. 4).
diversity_detail.notes: Contrast directions are reversed from homogenisation to represent diversity; the reported means and SDs retain the paper's original homogenisation scale. The abstract's statement that No AI achieved the highest level of creativity is a narrative interpretation: the complete Results section supplies no separate creativity instrument, rating, score, or test (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3-4, IV. Results).

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1 is met by the explicit Methods statement that 36 graduate students were randomly assigned to the three AI-access conditions (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology), despite the abstract's quasi-experimental label (PDF p. 1, Abstract). Criterion 2 is not met: the entire assigned cohort is 36 people, below 50; analyzed-person and per-arm people counts are not stated. Criterion 3 is met by homogenisation scored on the final products of 13 collaborative groups (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and IV. Results; p. 4, IV. Results). Under codebook section 3, randomized experiments below 50 people belong in the screening report and are omitted from the dataset, so this study is neither core nor observational context. Flag for two-screener review because Methods report random assignment.

one_line_finding: In a study reporting random assignment of 36 graduate students (13 collaborative groups), mean homogenisation was 33.250 (SD = 7.932) for Immediate AI, 26.250 (SD = 4.272) for Delayed AI, and 17.800 (SD = 8.379) for No AI, with no numerical inferential tests or separate creativity score reported (Zenodo PDF, p. 3, III. Methodology; pp. 3-4, IV. Results).
notes: The abstract calls the design quasi-experimental, whereas Methods explicitly report random assignment. design_class is other only because the form has no unspecified-RCT category and the setting is insufficiently described to choose lab_rct, online_rct, or field_rct; assignment.randomized is yes (PDF p. 1, Abstract; pp. 2-3, III. Methodology). The individual assignment unit follows the stated assignment of students, but the randomization procedure and relationship to group formation remain unexplained. Flag for two-screener review despite the small sample. The French Rivera is the task location and does not establish participants' country. Figure 3 gives pooled thematic frequencies within the same homogenisation analysis, with no condition-specific contrast; it is not a separate creativity measure (PDF p. 3, III. Methodology and IV. Results).
